title: Ansgar's mission to Birka
description: The Frankish monk Ansgar preaches at the trading town of Birka, the first recorded Christian mission to the Swedes.

title: Archbishopric of Uppsala founded
description: Sweden receives its own archbishop, making its church independent of the Danish see of Lund.

title: Stockholm first mentioned
description: Letters of Birger Jarl give the first record of Stockholm, which he is traditionally said to have founded.

title: Kalmar Union
description: Eric of Pomerania is crowned king of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, joining the three kingdoms under one crown.

title: Meeting at Arboga
description: During Engelbrekt's rebellion against the Union king an assembly of the estates meets at Arboga, often called the first Riksdag.

title: Battle of Brunkeberg
description: The regent Sten Sture the Elder defeats Christian I of Denmark, keeping Sweden in effect self-governing within the Union.

title: Uppsala University founded
description: The first university in the Nordic countries is founded at Uppsala.

title: Stockholm Bloodbath
description: After his coronation Christian II of Denmark has about a hundred Swedish nobles and churchmen executed, which sets off the revolt that ends the Union.

title: Gustav Vasa elected king
description: The leader of the revolt against Denmark is elected king, the date now kept as Sweden's national day.

title: Riksdag of Västerås
description: The estates transfer church property to the crown and break with Rome, beginning the Swedish Reformation.

title: Reval submits to Sweden
description: The city of Reval and the nobility of northern Estonia accept Swedish rule, the first step of Sweden's Baltic empire.

title: Sinking of the Vasa
description: The new warship Vasa capsizes minutes into her maiden voyage; raised in 1961, she is now the best-preserved ship of her century.

title: Battle of Breitenfeld
description: Gustavus Adolphus defeats the Imperial army under Tilly, the first great Protestant victory of the Thirty Years' War.

title: Battle of Lützen
description: The Swedish army beats Wallenstein's but Gustavus Adolphus is killed, leaving the six-year-old Christina as queen.

title: Treaty of Roskilde
description: After Charles X Gustav marches his army across the frozen Belts, Denmark cedes Scania and other provinces, giving Sweden its greatest extent.

title: Charles XI's Reduction
description: The Riksdag lets the king take back crown lands from the high nobility, the basis of royal absolutism in Sweden.

title: Battle of Narva
description: Charles XII relieves Narva and routs a much larger Russian army in a snowstorm at the start of the Great Northern War.

title: Death of Charles XII
description: The king is shot dead while besieging a Norwegian fortress, bringing the end of the war and of Sweden's time as a great power.

title: Age of Liberty begins
description: A new Instrument of Government ends absolutism and passes power to the Riksdag for half a century.

title: Academy of Sciences founded
description: Carl Linnaeus and five others found the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

title: Freedom of the Press Act
description: Sweden abolishes most censorship and gives the public a right to see official documents, the first law of its kind.

title: Coup of Gustav III
description: The king takes power from the Riksdag without bloodshed, ending the Age of Liberty.

title: Gustav III shot
description: The king is shot by a noble conspirator at a masked ball at the opera and dies two weeks later.

title: Instrument of Government of 1809
description: After the loss of Finland and the overthrow of Gustav IV Adolf, a constitution divides power between king and Riksdag; it stays in force until 1974.

title: Bernadotte elected crown prince
description: The Riksdag chooses the French marshal Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte as heir to the throne, founding the dynasty that still reigns.

title: Treaty of Kiel
description: Denmark cedes Norway to the king of Sweden, leading after a short war to a union of the two kingdoms; Sweden has fought no war since.

title: Two-chamber Riksdag
description: The four medieval estates are replaced by a parliament of two chambers.

title: First Nobel Prizes
description: The first prizes endowed by Alfred Nobel's will are awarded on the anniversary of his death.

title: Union with Norway dissolved
description: Oscar II renounces the Norwegian throne after negotiations at Karlstad, ending the union peacefully.

title: First election with women voting
description: Women vote and are elected to the Riksdag for the first time, completing the move to universal suffrage.

title: Ådalen shootings
description: Soldiers fire on a workers' demonstration and kill five people, a turning point in Swedish labour relations.

title: Social Democrats take office
description: Per Albin Hansson forms the government that begins 44 years of Social Democratic rule and the building of the welfare state.

title: Saltsjöbaden Agreement
description: Employers and trade unions agree to settle disputes by negotiation without the state, the basis of the Swedish labour model.

title: Switch to driving on the right
description: On Dagen H all traffic in Sweden changes from the left to the right side of the road.

title: Olof Palme assassinated
description: The prime minister is shot dead in the street while walking home from a cinema.

title: Sweden joins the European Union
description: Sweden enters the European Union with Austria and Finland after a referendum in 1994.

title: Euro rejected in referendum
description: Voters decide to keep the krona, days after the murder of the foreign minister Anna Lindh.
